Done. `out/T4/model.safetensors` written on the first execution — 244 tensors, 64 merged.

**Approach:** a plain `safetensors` + `torch` script (`out/T4/solution.py`). I considered mergekit's `task_arithmetic`, which computes this exact formula, but it merges every tensor rather than a named 64, gives no way to enforce the bit-exact equality of the 180 untouched tensors or the "exactly 64 merged" check, and would round-trip through a HF model that could perturb tensors that must stay bit-exact.

**Ordering:** all three checkpoints are read up front and `base` is never written into, so both task vectors are taken against the unmodified base.

**Checks that fail the run:** identical key sets and 244 base tensors; matching shapes/dtypes; all 64 MLP names present and the set is exactly 64; every non-MLP tensor bit-identical across base/ft1/ft2; exactly 64 merged; 244 in the output; plus a post-write re-read confirming the count, the key set, and that nothing outside the MLP set differs from base.

Arithmetic in float32, cast back to each tensor's base dtype; untouched tensors copied bit-exactly.
